sources.citation: Suárez, Jorge A. 1990 [posthumous]. La clasificación de las lenguas zapotecas. In Beatriz Garza Cuarón & Paulette Levy (eds.), Homenaje a Jorge A. Suárez: lingüística indoamericana e hispánica (Estudios de Lingüística y Literatura, 18), 41-68. México: El Colegio de México. (Open-access scan, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, COLMEX Colecciones Digitales hdl 20.500.11986/COLMEX/10004199 = JSTOR j.ctv47w9zk.6.)
sources.note: Nothing explicit for any single variety; family-level remarks only: post-tonic/final vowels lost completely around Mitla, devoiced nearer Oaxaca City, still voiced at Chichicapam (isoglosses 1-2); 'pérdida de vocales pretónicas' follows the same patterns; tone reconstruction lacking (p. 50). For Mazaltepec: intermediate stage of the isogloss-6 *t change with slight frication, and a peculiar loss of word-initial /g/ before /a/, /u/; lexical isogloss membership for nube/raíz/hueso (fn. 11) and cuadro 2.

sources.note: The SIL intelligibility survey that established Mazaltepec as a separate variety (Ethnologue's source); no phonology expected, but it names the test texts/recordings and may point to an SIL wordlist for Santo Tomás Mazaltepec.
sources.venue: La inteligibilidad interdialectal en México: Resultados de algunos sondeos

sources.citation: Suárez, Jorge A. 1972. La clasificación del papabuco y del solteco. Anuario de Letras (México: UNAM, Facultad de Filosofía y Letras) 10: 219-232.
sources.note: Only the transcription convention ('Con ' se indica el acento') and stress-conditioned environments in the sound laws (*kw > /p/ geminate after the tonic vowel, /kʷ/ before it; /t/ for *t before *i in post-tonic position in several Valley dialects); establishes that Suárez personally collected Mazaltepec Zapotec data c. 1970 and that Mazaltepec has the fortis geminate (zissu).
sources.venue: Anuario de Letras (México: UNAM, Facultad de Filosofía y Letras)
